crime_highlights: Jeffery Blair Borden has pled guilty to trafficking 378 grams of cocaine and possession of 2,042 unstamped cigarettes
Mr. Borden told police that whatever they find belongs to him
A search of the dwelling led to the seizure of the following items, all of which were possessed by Jeffrey Borden
rationale_highlights: systemic barriers, such as limited educational and employment opportunities within a marginalized community, contribute to cycles of financial instability, substance use, and emotional strain
Overall, the IRCA provides support to find reduced moral blameworthiness on the part of Mr. Borden
Considering Mr. Borden’s reduced moral blameworthiness based on the content of the IRCA, I do not believe a sentence as lengthy and harsh as that proposed by the Crown is necessary or appropriate
note: Drug trafficking; no victim harm in facts.

crime_highlights: Adam Drake stabbed Pat Stay in the chest one time
In stabbing Pat Stay, Adam Drake knew that he would cause serious bodily harm that would likely result in death
Pat Stay died from a single stab wound to the chest
Adam Drake left the place of the stabbing before he knew the condition of the victim
rationale_highlights: He was the victim of trauma at the hands of persons in authority outside of the household
Many identifiable systemic discriminatory factors have influenced and plagued his youth and adult life
I have considered the appropriate mitigation related to the Gladue factors as described by Justice Hunt in Sylliboy
note: Court notes mitigation considered but never states effect on culpability.

crime_highlights: The Accused attacked the Victim with the knife in the kitchen
First, he slashed her from her left ear, down the side of her neck, onto her chest and under her right breast
the Accused stabbed her in the back with the same knife
She continued to run away from the Victim as she was afraid for her life
At this time she started to feel blood gurgle in her lungs
rationale_highlights: I agree with Mr. Berrigan; I have seen a number of these, and it is one that I can say was very important to the outcome here
Dominic Caldi’s story exemplifies the intersection of racial trauma, mental illness and systemic neglect

The court is therefore urged to craft a sentence that embodies Anderson’s vision. One that recognizes the moral blameworthiness of the offence while refusing to perpetrate the structural inequities that produced it.
note: Principle quote highlighted in full from IRCA; para 24 included.
